stories.headline: Anthropic Plans $200M Investment in PE Venture to Sell AI Tools to Portfolio Companies

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is planning to invest $200 million in a new venture with major private-equity firms that aims to sell AI tools to their portfolio companies.
General Atlantic, Blackstone, and Hellman & Friedman are among the PE firms in discussions to back the project, with Anthropic in talks to raise $1 billion for the effort.
The new company would serve as a consulting arm for Anthropic that teaches businesses how to incorporate Claude AI tools in their operations.
OpenAI is also in talks to form a rival joint venture with PE firms called DeployCo, having reassigned its COO to work on the project.
Anthropic last month announced a separate $100 million effort to provide training and technical support for consulting firms helping enterprises adopt Claude.

stories.headline: Anthropic Hits $30B Run-Rate Revenue, Signs 3.5GW TPU Deal With Google and Broadcom

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's run-rate revenue has surpassed $30 billion, up from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025, tripling in roughly four months.
Anthropic signed a deal with Google and Broadcom for approximately 3.5 gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity, starting in 2027.
Business customers spending over $1 million annually now exceed 1,000, doubling from 500 in less than two months since the Series G announcement in February.
Broadcom's regulatory filing includes a risk disclosure noting that Anthropic's consumption of the expanded compute is 'dependent on Anthropic's continued commercial success.'
Broadcom will develop and supply future-generation TPUs for Google under a long-term agreement, with a supply assurance agreement for networking and rack components through 2031.
The vast majority of the new compute will be sited in the United States, expanding Anthropic's November 2025 commitment to invest $50 billion in American computing infrastructure.

Anthropic confirmed it trains and runs Claude on a range of hardware — AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, and NVIDIA GPUs — and remains available on all three major cloud platforms: AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

stories.headline: Apple App Store New Apps Surge 84% in Q1 2026 as AI Coding Tools Reverse Decade-Long Decline

key_facts.fact: New applications listed globally on Apple's App Store surged 84% year-over-year to 235,800 in Q1 2026, according to Sensor Tower data.
The growth reverses a decade-long decline: new App Store applications had cumulatively fallen by 48% between 2016 and 2024 before rebounding 30% in 2025.
The primary driver is AI-assisted 'vibe coding' tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex, which enable non-programmers to generate functional applications through text prompts.
Apple has taken regulatory measures against some native vibe coding applications and blocked vibe coding apps from updating their features after listing.
Sensor Tower Senior Analyst Abraham Yousef said the growth 'aligns closely with the widespread adoption of intelligent programming tools that can eliminate application development barriers.'

stories.headline: Artemis II Completes Historic Lunar Flyby, Shatters Apollo 13 Distance Record by 4,101 Miles

key_facts.fact: Orion spacecraft surpassed the Apollo 13 distance record of 248,655 miles at 17:56 UTC on April 6, reaching a maximum distance of 252,756 miles (406,771 km) from Earth
The crew made closest approach to the Moon at 4,067 miles above the lunar surface and experienced a 40-minute communications blackout behind the far side
The crew witnessed a total solar eclipse as the Moon blocked the Sun, and saw the landing sites of Apollo 12 and 14 during their flyby
Apollo 13 commander Jim Lovell's recorded farewell message was beamed to the crew; Lovell had died last August, two months after the recording
Trump congratulated the crew in a live link-up, calling it 'really big stuff' while the White House had proposed cutting NASA's budget by $5.6 billion just days earlier
The crew—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Jeremy Hansen—are now on a return path to Earth with splashdown set for Friday

stories.headline: Broadcom Signs Deal to Produce Google TPUs Through 2031, Expands Anthropic Compute to 3.5 GW

key_facts.fact: Broadcom agreed to produce future versions of Google's AI chips and provide networking equipment for next-gen AI data racks through 2031, per SEC filing
Anthropic will receive approximately 3.5 gigawatts of next-generation TPU-based computing capacity starting in 2027
Anthropic's run-rate revenue surpassed $30 billion, up from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025
Over 1,000 business customers now spending more than $1 million annually on Claude, doubling from February in less than two months
Mizuho analysts estimated Broadcom would pick up $21 billion in AI revenue from Anthropic in 2026 and $42 billion in 2027
Vast majority of new compute will be sited in the US, expanding Anthropic's November 2025 commitment to invest $50 billion in American computing infrastructure
Broadcom shares rose 3% in extended trading following the announcement

stories.headline: Taiwan Intelligence: China Targeting Island's Chip Tech and Talent to Break 'Containment'

key_facts.fact: Taiwan's National Security Bureau report to lawmakers says China is attempting to 'lure' Taiwan's AI and semiconductor industries to establish operations in China
China using indirect channels to poach talent, steal technology, and procure controlled goods to obtain advanced-process chips and break 'international technological containment'
11 new mainland Chinese firms were put under investigation by Taiwan's Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau for illegally poaching semiconductor talent
100 cases of Chinese talent poaching have been handled by Taiwan's MJIB since 2020, including a probe into SMIC last year
Taiwan's Government Service Network was targeted by more than 170 million intrusion attempts in Q1 2026
Over 420 Chinese military aircraft were detected operating around Taiwan in Q1, with 10 joint combat readiness patrols

stories.headline: Nvidia-Backed Firmus Raises $505M at $5.5B Valuation for Asia-Pacific AI Data Centers

key_facts.fact: Australian AI infrastructure startup Firmus raised $505 million led by Coatue Management with Nvidia participation, at a $5.5 billion post-money valuation
Firmus has raised $1.35 billion in the last six months, including this latest transaction, and is preparing for an ASX IPO later this year
Project Southgate aims to build a network of AI data centers across Australia with capacity up to 1.6 gigawatts over the next three years, in collaboration with Nvidia and CDC Data Centres
Tasmania facility will house 36,000 Nvidia accelerator chips after first two rounds of technology deployments, using Nvidia's Vera Rubin DSX reference design
Also backed by Blackstone, which extended $10 billion in debt financing in February
Firmus has already deployed facilities in Singapore through a partnership with ST Telemedia Global Data Centres, backed by Temasek

stories.headline: Intel in Talks With Google and Amazon for Advanced EMIB Chip Packaging Services

key_facts.fact: Intel has been in ongoing discussions with Google and Amazon to provide advanced chip packaging services through its Foundry division, per Wired citing multiple sources
Intel's EMIB and EMIB-T packaging technology is positioned as a more power-efficient and cost-effective alternative to TSMC's CoWoS, which is severely supply-constrained
EMIB-T is set to roll out in Intel fabs this year, with mass production already being prepared at the Rio Rancho, New Mexico facility
Intel Foundry chief Naga Chandrasekaran said a rise in capital expenditure will be the clearest signal that major customers have signed on
Intel executives say packaging revenue could reach well north of $1 billion and eventually run into multi-billion-dollar annual deals
Potential customers are cautious, worried Intel may not deliver on expansion promises or that TSMC could cut their wafer allocations in response

stories.headline: Iran Rejects 45-Day Ceasefire, Submits 10-Point Plan as Trump Tuesday Deadline Looms

key_facts.fact: Iran rejected the 45-day ceasefire proposal and submitted a 10-point plan through Pakistan demanding a permanent end to the war, not a temporary truce
Iran's 10-point framework includes demands for ending regional conflicts, safe Strait of Hormuz passage, reconstruction of war-affected areas, and lifting international sanctions
Trump acknowledged Iran's proposal as 'a significant step' but said 'it's not good enough' and threatened to destroy every bridge and power plant in Iran by Tuesday midnight
Iran's chief negotiator said Iran no longer trusts the Trump administration after the US bombed the Republic twice during previous rounds of talks
Defense Secretary Hegseth said Monday would see the 'largest volume of strikes since day one' with even more the next day
The UN warned any attack on civilian infrastructure is a clear violation of international law; a US-Israeli projectile struck a synagogue in Tehran
A regional official involved in talks said diplomatic efforts had not collapsed: 'We are still talking to both sides'

stories.headline: Israel Deepens Lebanon Offensive With Renewed Strikes Across Country, 15+ Killed in One Day

key_facts.fact: Israeli forces launched renewed airstrikes across Lebanon on Sunday April 6, hitting the south and Beirut's outskirts, killing at least 15 people in a single day
A strike in the Christian area of Ain Saadeh east of Beirut killed three people including Pierre Moawad, a member of the anti-Hezbollah Lebanese Forces party, and his wife
A strike in Beirut's Jnah neighbourhood landed about 100 meters from the Rafik Hariri University Hospital, Lebanon's largest public facility, killing 5 and wounding 52
Since March 2, Israeli attacks on Lebanon have killed more than 1,500 people including 130 children and displaced over 1.2 million
Israeli military chief Lt Gen Eyal Zamir visited troops in southern Lebanon and pledged to intensify strikes against Hezbollah
Experts warn Israel aims to deepen fissures between Lebanese communities by expanding strikes beyond Shia areas into Christian neighborhoods

stories.headline: Kalshi Wins Landmark Third Circuit Appeal: Federal Law Preempts State Gambling Regulation

key_facts.fact: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 2-1 that New Jersey cannot bring enforcement action against Kalshi, finding the federal Commodity Exchange Act preempts state gambling laws
The court held that Kalshi's self-certified sports-related event contracts are 'presumptively approved' because the CFTC has not found them contrary to the public interest
The dissenting judge argued the products 'are sports gambling,' citing NFL game outcome bets, point spreads, and player prop contracts available on the platform
Sports-related event contracts represent approximately 85% of Kalshi's business; the ruling aligns with earlier decisions in Nevada and Tennessee but conflicts with Maryland and Massachusetts rulings
Kalshi still faces pending legal challenges in Ohio, Connecticut, and New York, with the circuit split likely heading toward Supreme Court review

stories.headline: Meta Preparing New AI Models Under Alexandr Wang, Will Delay Open-Source Release

key_facts.fact: Meta is preparing to release the first AI models developed under Alexandr Wang, the Scale AI founder acquired by Meta, with plans to offer open-source versions of those models.
Meta will not open-source the models immediately or in full, keeping certain components private for safety and competitive reasons — a subtle shift from its historical open-source approach.
Meta's previous Llama 4 family fell behind competitors, and the company delayed a model release last month due to concerns it was still underperforming.
Wang sees Meta as a way to provide widely accessible, US-built AI models for developers and consumers, unlike OpenAI and Anthropic which mainly target businesses and governments.

stories.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Share Intel to Detect Adversarial Model Distillation

key_facts.fact: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are sharing information through the Frontier Model Forum to detect adversarial distillation attempts that violate their terms of service.
US officials have estimated that unauthorised distillation costs Silicon Valley labs billions of dollars in annual profit.
OpenAI confirmed its participation and pointed to a memo it sent to Congress accusing DeepSeek of trying to 'free-ride on the capabilities developed by OpenAI and other US frontier labs.'
Information sharing on distillation remains limited due to AI companies' uncertainty about what can be shared under existing antitrust guidance.
The Frontier Model Forum was founded in 2023 by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft as an industry nonprofit.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches Safety Fellowship Hours After New Yorker Exposes Dissolved Safety Teams

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced the Safety Fellowship, a five-month pilot program for external researchers to pursue safety and alignment research, running September 14, 2026 through February 5, 2027.
Priority research areas include safety evaluation, robustness, scalable mitigations, privacy-preserving safety methods, agentic oversight, and high-severity misuse domains.

The fellowship was announced hours after The New Yorker published an investigation reporting that OpenAI had dissolved its superalignment and AGI-readiness teams and dropped safety from its IRS Form 990 filings.
The Mission Alignment team, successor to Superalignment, was disbanded in February 2026 after 16 months; by early 2026 the people most associated with safety oversight had largely departed.
Fellows will receive API credits and mentorship but will not have internal system access; applications close May 3 with notifications by July 25.

stories.headline: Samsung Posts Record Q1 Operating Profit of 57.2 Trillion Won ($38B), Up 755% YoY

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics reported preliminary Q1 operating profit of 57.2 trillion won ($38B), surging 755% from 6.61 trillion won a year earlier
Quarterly revenue hit 133 trillion won, up 68.1% YoY, exceeding 100 trillion won for the first time ever; Q1 operating profit alone exceeded full-year 2025 earnings of 43.6 trillion won
Results crushed market expectations: operating profit was 36.7% above the average analyst estimate, driven by surging AI memory chip demand
DRAM contract prices rose 90-95% in Q1 and are projected to climb another 60% in Q2, with some forecasts pointing to 250% annual price surge
Analysts project Samsung could surpass Nvidia next year in annual operating profit; KB Securities raised annual forecast to 327 trillion won for 2026

stories.headline: Samsung Reports Record $38B Q1 Operating Profit, 8x YoY, on AI Memory Chip Boom

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics estimated Q1 2026 operating profit of 57.2 trillion won ($37.92 billion), more than 8x the 6.69 trillion won a year earlier, far exceeding the LSEG SmartEstimate of 40.6 trillion won.
The record-high results nearly triple Samsung's previous record quarterly operating profit of 20 trillion won, reached in Q4 2025.
Revenue jumped 68% year-over-year to 133 trillion won, also beating consensus forecasts of 119 trillion won.

Samsung's chip division generated an estimated 54 trillion won in operating profit, accounting for 95% of total profit; the AI boom has constrained supply for traditional chips and led to near-doubling of chip prices in Q1.

TrendForce expects contract DRAM prices to increase more than 50% in Q2 as the shortage persists, with Samsung's soaring earnings coming mainly from the rebound in commodity chip demand fueled by AI inference.

stories.headline: SpaceX Plans $75B IPO at Up to $1.75T Valuation With Unprecedented Retail Investor Push

key_facts.fact: SpaceX plans to raise $75 billion in the largest IPO ever, targeting a valuation of up to $1.75 trillion, with roadshow launching the week of June 8
CFO Bret Johnsen told the full 21-bank syndicate that 'retail is going to be a critical part of this and a bigger part than any IPO in history'
SpaceX will host 1,500 retail investors at a major event on June 11, with retail investors in the US, UK, EU, Australia, Canada, Japan, and Korea eligible to participate
Musk previously sought to set aside up to 30% of shares for retail investors, compared with 5-10% for most IPOs; the IPO prospectus is planned for late May
Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Citigroup, JPMorgan, and Goldman Sachs are leading the deal with 16 other banks in smaller roles
The $1.75T target is a significant step up from the $1.25T combined valuation set when SpaceX merged with Musk's AI startup xAI in February
